summary.headline: Kamdhenu FY26 PBT rose 31% to INR106 crore on 10% franchisee volume growth and 25% royalty income growth to INR175 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 was a year of volume growth and higher royalty per ton, with franchisee volume up 10% to 37.9 lakh MT and royalty income up 25% to INR175 crore. Total revenue grew only 2% to INR763 crore, as TMT average selling prices were marginally softer YoY. Q4 FY26 showed royalty income up 19% to INR46 crore and PBT up 8% to INR24 crore, while own-manufacturing volume was flat. The company remains debt-free and proposed a dividend of INR0.40 per share.

financial_highlights.value: INR0.40 per share (40% of INR1 face value)

segments.name: Franchisee royalty (asset-light)
segments.commentary: Royalty income INR175 crore in FY26 on 37.9 lakh MT; average royalty rate rose to INR435/MT from INR398/MT, about 10% higher. Management guides to 10-15% annual royalty rate increases plus about 10% volume growth.

segments.name: Own manufacturing (Delhi-NCR plant)
segments.commentary: Single plant with about 1.25 lakh MT capacity running at 100% utilisation in FY25 and FY26; volume 121,092 MT in FY26, flat YoY. Top line is driven by steel price pass-through, and management says bottom line is mainly from royalty.

guidance_outlook: Royalty per ton to rise 10-15% every year, alongside around 10% franchisee volume growth.
Management expects steel demand growth to sustain and potentially accelerate over the medium term, citing INR12.2 lakh crore central capital outlay.
Near-term margin pressure flagged from crude oil and natural gas costs and geopolitical volatility, affecting the company and franchisees.
Focus for FY27 is brand investment, expanding volumes at existing franchisees, and adding franchisees in South India.
Treasury policy for about INR300 crore of cash being framed; management says it will be used only for steel business and shareholder rewards.
Franchise capacity data to be released in Q1 FY27 after compilation; existing capacity cited at around 5 million MT versus 4 million MT in the old presentation.
risks_watch: Revenue growth (2%) lagged profit growth (31%) as TMT prices softened; watch whether pricing recovers.
Raw material cost volatility (crude, natural gas, iron ore) may pressure margins for the company and franchisees.
Q4 PAT growth slowed to 2% despite royalty income up 19%.
Franchisee capacity and utilisation data pending for Q1 FY27; the previous figures were called outdated.
Use of about INR300 crore cash and the treasury/shareholder reward policy remains undefined.
Own plant at 100% utilisation limits volume growth from that asset; price pass-through drives its top line.
summary.management_tone: Confident on brand, royalty model and demand outlook, but evasive on specifics: no numeric FY27 guidance, deferred capacity data and treasury plans, and some answers were unclear or contradictory.
key_quotes: This royalty led revenue model is in our view, the defining financial characteristic of Kamdhenu's business, and we expect it to contribute an increasingly larger proportion of our overall earnings over the coming years.
We are charging royalty on per ton basis, not on the percentage basis. So the price fluctuation is not impacting our business at all, either in own manufacturing or in the branding business.
Going forward, we are also planning to increase 10% to 15% every year along with a volume growth of around 10%, which we are achieving from last 2, 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did royalty income grow 25% when franchisee volume grew only 10% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the royalty rate per ton was raised, so revenue growth (25%) outpaced volume growth (10%); average royalty rose to INR435/MT from INR398/MT.

qa_highlights.question: What are the royalty per ton trend and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Only FY25 and FY26 figures were available (INR398 and INR435/MT, about 10% up); earlier level cited at around INR380/MT. Going forward royalty is planned to rise 10-15% every year with about 10% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: What will be done with the roughly INR300 crore of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a treasury policy is being framed on how to reward shareholders and will be revert later; no figure or timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was about INR20 crore invested in the paint business in March 2026, and will there be more?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment bought a 4% equity stake at a low share price relative to the business valuation; management said there are no plans for further infusion, and treasury will be used only for steel and shareholder rewards.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin guidance for own manufacturing versus royalty in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no numeric guidance; the single plant at about 1.25 lakh MT runs at 100% utilisation, top line moves with steel price, and bottom line is mainly royalty-driven.

qa_highlights.question: How are franchise additions and volume growth split between existing and new units, and what is the FY27 pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focusing on volume growth at existing units, not adding new ones; about 4-5 units exited and 4-5 were added in FY26 across roughly 100 units, with South India as the exception for new additions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current franchisee capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the presented data was an outdated compilation; existing capacity is around 5 million MT versus 3.9 million MT volume, with fresh data to be released in Q1 FY27.

capex_capacity: Own plant: single Delhi-NCR plant, capacity about 1.25 lakh MT, run at 100% utilisation in FY25 and FY26; management expects 100% utilisation to continue near term.

Franchise network: about 100 units in total, of which about 50 manufacture TMT bars and about 50 make structural steel pipe, colour-coated sheet and other products; roughly 4-5 units exited and 4-5 new units added in FY26.

Franchise capacity: old presentation showed over 4 million MT against 3.9 million MT volume; management said existing capacity is around 5 million MT and the revised compilation will be released in Q1 FY27 after documents are compiled.
FY27 focus is on expanding capacity of existing franchisee units and adding franchisees in South India; no new-unit addition push outside the South.
demand_pricing: Steel demand: India saw high single-digit steel consumption growth in FY26; management expects demand to sustain and potentially accelerate over the medium term, citing INR12.2 lakh crore central capital outlay, National Steel Policy and affordable housing, smart cities and urban/rural infrastructure.

Pricing: TMT average selling prices were marginally softer YoY in FY26, which management attributed to the broader steel sector pricing environment and called temporary; royalty is charged per ton, so price moves do not affect royalty income.
Royalty realisation: average royalty rose to INR435/MT in FY26 from INR398/MT in FY25 (about 10%); earlier level was around INR380/MT; management plans 10-15% annual increases.

Raw materials: domestic iron ore prices trended up on domestic demand while global iron ore was stable; crude oil and natural gas volatility from geopolitical disruption is expected to pressure margins for the company and franchisees near term.
Regional volume mix: North 31%, East 35%, West 19%, South 15% of overall volume; management plans to raise share in the South.
Competition: national peers named as Tata Steel and Jindal; regional brands cited as reasonably strong; management claims a 12,500-dealer network can supply volume at short notice.
Market share: estimated retail branded market share of about 20% for Kamdhenu; exact TMT market data not available.
Brand premium: management cited an average premium of about INR2,600/ton, with some states at INR6,000/ton extra and others at INR1,500-2,000/ton.

adds.what: Franchise network: no new-unit addition push outside South; FY27 focus on expanding capacity of existing franchisee units and adding franchisees in South India

growth.why: Management guides ~10% franchisee volume growth plus 10-15% annual royalty rate increases from FY27, backed by high-single-digit steel demand and a franchise capacity of ~5 million MT (compilation due Q1 FY27), but own plant is at 100% utilisation with no new units planned and no specific capacity additions quantified.
